title: The Gift of Encouragement
verse: The brothers from there, when they heard about us, came as far as the Forum of Appius and Three Taverns to meet us. When he saw them, Paul thanked God and took courage.
observation: Have you ever had someone in your life that was hard when it was time for gift giving? You loved this person, but you never knew what to give them. There is one gift that never gets old and is always welcomed by everyone. That gift is encouragement. When Paul arrived in Rome, it was at the end of a long journey. Also, Paul’s journey was not complete. He had not yet met with Caesar. However, when he saw the church in Rome, they gave Paul the greatest gift you can give a weary traveler. He received encouragement. Who do you need to give the gift of encouragement to today? Here are the ground rules. The first rule is to give it to someone you think needs it. The second rule is to write it down so they can look back at it when they need it the most. Rule three is to not expect anything in return. Rule four is to make the encouragement all about them. Do not insert yourself in any way. The final rule is to make sure it is sincere and specific. Watch what happens. I can guarantee it will bless your heart more than you can imagine. There is one word of warning. Many people are not good at receiving sincere encouragement. Therefore, do not judge your effectiveness based on their response. Be faithful and let God do what only He can do.
prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for loving us in such a way that it gives us the capacity to love others.
